Following the publication of the Voluntary Ex-Ante Notice (VEAT) on the 20th March 2023, the Authority has observed a voluntary 10-day standstill period from the publication date of the VEAT Notice and will now award the contract, pursuant to Regulation 99 (3) (c) of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 (as amended (EU Exit) 2020 etc.) EU Exit) Regulations 2020).

The contract value for a 36 month period is £1,048,170 Pound Sterling. The aggregate contract value or the 36 month period, including a 24 month extension, is £1,746,950 Pound Sterling. 

The contract award decision is as a result of a robust due diligence process undertaken as a negotiation without prior publication, under Regulation 32 (1) (b) of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 ("PCR 2015") (as amended The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020).

The Rapid Intervention Service (RIS) has been established in the West Essex area since 2017 and the RIS model is designed to deliver responsive interventions to patients in their own home which otherwise would have led to a presentation at A&E in an acute setting and to decrease unnecessary emergency ambulance conveyances in Harlow, Epping North Loughton, Buckhurst Hill and Chigwell areas.

The contract duration is from 01st April 2023 - 30th March 2026, with the option to extend for a further 24 months. The aggregate total contract value, including all options, is £1,746,950.00 Pound Sterling.

The purpose of this notice is to inform the market of an awarded contract to WHZAN by Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board to deliver a supportive telehealth system which links with all appropriate clinical systems.

The equipment will help to conduct multiple comprehensive assessments through the measurements of vital signs, recording photos, performing multiple assessments and questionnaires including NEWS2.  Through the implementation of this equipment, signs of deterioration or illness are identified earlier for a clinical response or increased carer support.

The equipment will b provided to Care Homes within the Epping, Loughton, Buckhurst Hill & Chigwell and Harlow localities, based on need.

The contract is for the period of 1-year and is being used as a pilot to understand the impact for patients in using this equipment.  This evaluation will determine whether there is a requirement for a longer-term solution.

The contract value is £32,000 (excluding VAT), £38,000 (including VAT).

title: 9114  List Condition and Engagement Project Phase 2  East of England  - AWARD
description:
Historic England is seeking to engage with community groups and organisations (and through them a wider pool of volunteers) based in, or working within, the Local Authority Districts of Tendring, Luton, Southend-on-Sea or Harlow, on an important piece of work which we are undertaking.  
      
      The project aims are to support ongoing work to improve engagement opportunities with the National Heritage List for England (NHLE) which is more commonly known as the List. In 2021-22, three pilot projects undertaken with external partners, such as civic or amenity societies, assessed the condition of the List in three selected areas.
       
      As well as helping us to improve our understanding of issues and limitations with the information contained within the List, this second phase of projects will help more people and communities connect with, and better understand, the extent and value of their local heritage. The work will help familiarise you and your team of volunteers with the regimes in place to help protect and promote this heritage, while giving you closer involvement with the designated heritage of your own area.

title: CO0587 - Essex ActivAte Programme (HAF) 2025
description:
The Department for Education has provided Essex County Council with funding in order to deliver the holiday activity and food programme (HAF) across Essex during the Easter, Summer and Winter school holidays. Active Essex will be managing the programme on behalf of Essex County Council. Active Essex and Essex County Council will also be managing the HAF programme on behalf of Thurrock Council. Across Essex and Thurrock the programme is called Essex ActvAte. \r
\r
Essex ActivAte will engage and support young people and families who are eligible for benefits based free school meals and families most in need. The programme will provide free and inclusive holiday clubs across the county that will include a range of fun physical and enrichment activities, a free nutritious meal, nutritional education and mentoring and support for the young person and whole family. The programme aims to improve health generally, including, crucially, mental health and aim to provide the families with the knowledge and support to live healthier, happier lives.  \r
\r
We are looking for delivery partners or consortiums who can lead and deliver Essex ActivAte clubs across Essex and Thurrock during the main school holidays.  \r
\r
The Essex ActivAte programme has now been running for 3 years, working with over 300 delivery partners to offer over 150,000 free spaces and hot meals per year. Over the next year of 2025, it is our aim to extend the programme so that every young person who is eligible for benefits based free school meals or is in need of this holiday support has the opportunity to engage in a local club. \r
\r
Key outcomes of each Essex ActivAte club are:\r
â€¢	To provide free and inclusive holiday activity clubs for eligible young people\r
â€¢	To provide a safe environment for young people to attend in the school holidays\r
â€¢	To provide a fun, high quality holiday club experience for the young people\r
â€¢	To support the social skills of the young people attending\r
â€¢	To provide mentors and role model through the Essex ActivAte club staff\r
â€¢	To ensure that young people have at least 1 nutritious meal each day\r
â€¢	To provide education for the young people and whole family around eating more healthy, nutritious meals, on a budget\r
â€¢	Providing signposting and support for the whole family so that they have the understanding and knowledge to improve their physical and mental health and wellbeing, support network and opportunities. \r
\r
The maximum bid value per project is £300,000.

title: Heritage Works for Creative Businesses (NP 234) - AWARD
description:
The aim of this follow-on research is to offer guidance and encouragement to investors interested in taking on unused or under-used historic buildings with a view to converting them for use by creative businesses, which form one of the key growth sectors in the UK economy and which are therefore likely to be expanding in the next few years. 
      
      The objectives can be expressed in terms of three questions:
      1. How and to what extent have historic buildings added value to creative businesses?
      This would involve analysis of creative uses such as the Custard Factory in Digbeth, the Hat Factory in Luton, Hotwalls in Portsmouth and the Biscuit Factory in Ouseburn, highlighting both the contribution made to the success of these places by their historic character and the value derived from it. Substantive case studies are not required here but will instead be commissioned separately.
      
      2. Where in England do the favourable circumstances combine to suggest that creative businesses could be attracted to locate there when growing?
      
      In a similar way as done for the north of England by GC Insight, this section would look at where the non-heritage vital ingredients for creative businesses overlap with heritage opportunity areas such that, with appropriate planning policies and financing models, these localities would make good nurseries for growing creative businesses. It would also highlight opportunities for heritage attractions to serve not as premises for creative businesses but as anchor sites - as footfall generators or showcases/outlets for the products of neighbouring creative businesses.
      
      3. In favourable localities, what help might commercial developers, building preservation trusts and community development trusts need to bring to the market sustainable, inspiring and affordable historic premises attractive to creative businesses looking to expand?
      
      This section would adapt the recent 'Heritage Works for Housing' guidance to take into account the particular demands of creative businesses, such as flexible layouts, playful design, gigabit digital connectivity, communal areas, individual maker spaces and 'third spaces'.

title: Contract for the Provision of Coroner's Post Mortems
description:
This is an Award Notice. Hertfordshire County Council have awarded a contract for the Provision of Coroner's Post Mortems. There is no competition for this service. Deceased bodies referred to the Hertfordshire Coroner must remain within their jurisdiction until officially released by the Hertfordshire Coroner.

Hertfordshire County Council (HCC) is relying on Regulation 32(2)(b)(ii) of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 in making this award without prior publication. Regulation 32(2)(b)(ii) permits such an award where competition is absent for technical reasons.

The Local Authority has a statutory duty to provide a Coroner Service for the community of Hertfordshire.  As part of the Coroner's duties, he/she must establish a cause of death if none has been provided by the signing/authorising medical practitioner.  

To facilitate post-mortem examinations Hertfordshire County Council has contracts with local NHS Hospital mortuaries.  There are 3 NHS Hospital mortuaries within Hertfordshire (or close to the Hertfordshire border) that provide post-mortem services to the Coroner Service.  Currently, one mortuary would not be able to manage the volume of post-mortems requested by Hertfordshire so we need more than one contract to cover this requirement.

The direct award value of £980,000 reflects the total estimated value that will be awarded over the whole term of the contract between the three NHS trusts receiving the direct award.  The £980,000 will not be equally divided between the three NHS trusts but will be awarded based on volume of deceased sent to each NHS trust for coronial post-mortem examination each month.

Reg 32(2)(b) states that a procurement is not required where a service can only be supplied by a particular economic operator ENHT, WHHT and PAH in this case because "competition is absent for technical reasons".
